source.title: Few Tokens, Big Leverage: Preserving Safety Alignment by Constraining Safety Tokens during Fine-tuning
source.authors: Guoli Wang; Haonan Shi; Tu Ouyang; Angelina Wang

page_placements.theme: Safety processing depends on layers, heads and feature circuits

record.tranche_reason: The study fine-tunes safety-aligned models with harmful or benign downstream data and measures harmful-response rates, directly testing the fine-tuning and safety-behavior relationship in new settings.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports PACT-specific defenses and their comparisons; those method-comparison results are not cataloged as findings about the claim itself. It does not report position-wise aligned-versus-base KL divergence, compliant-opening prefills, adversarial-suffix or decoding bypass tests, or safety-weight/rank localization.
record.test_reason: Vanilla LoRA SFT of four instruct models on downstream tasks mixed with 250–500 AdvBench harmful examples raises judged ASR from near zero to 46–95% (V1). A benign-only AGNEWS run on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct (Table 4, P=0%) bears on V2. The other versions are not tested: no aligned-vs-base per-position KL, no inference-time prefill, suffix or decoding attacks, no weight or rank localization, and no deepening training.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is mostly right. The authors state that even benign fine-tuning weakens refusal and that small amounts of harmful data amplify this. They propose PACT, which regularizes confidence on a compact set of safety tokens, and report a better safety–utility trade-off. Their own benign-only result (Table 4, P=0%) shows essentially no safety drift, so the benign-erosion statement rests on cited prior work, not on their data.
record.recipe_differences: Uses downstream-task fine-tuning mixed with harmful data and evaluates harmful-response rates, but combines this with LoRA and downstream task datasets rather than presenting a direct replication of the original studies.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported outcomes vary across model, downstream dataset, harmful-data proportion, safety benchmark, and evaluator. The main evaluations use Llama-Guard-3-8B; the appendix also reports an alternative evaluator.

fits_no_version.finding: At inference, boosting the logits of 50 identified safety tokens cuts JailbreakBench ASR from 33.5% to 0.5%, and ablating them raises it to 41.5%. Random-token controls stay at 34–35%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal depends causally on a small vocabulary subset of safety tokens. This is token-level, not weight-level, localization.

fits_no_version.finding: Under harmful-mix SFT, average safety-token confidence falls alongside the safety rate. Safety-token logits at answer positions 1–4 collapse below the initial model's values.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Harmful fine-tuning suppresses refusal-token confidence at early response positions. Later positions are not compared, so this does not show concentration in early positions.

record.problems: The text reports no uncertainty estimates for the behavioral rates. Main results use a specified judge model, though an alternative evaluator is reported in the appendix. The benign-only comparison covers one model, one dataset, and three benchmarks.
record.rows_left_out: PACT-specific results and its comparisons with defense baselines are not included as claim findings. Figure 5 hyperparameter sweeps vary PACT calibration and safety-token count, not the claim's opening-prefill or decoding bypasses.

untested.parts: Only 250 or 500 harmful examples (5%/10%) mixed into 5,000 task examples, with LoRA rank 8. Not tested: very small counts (tens of examples), pure-harmful datasets, and full-parameter fine-tuning.
Benign-only SFT appears for one model (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct) on one dataset (AGNEWS). No identity-shifting or specially selected benign data is tested.
Not tested. No per-position aligned-vs-base KL is reported. Δt is aggregated over positions to select tokens.
Not tested. There is no inference-time prefill, suffix or decoding attack. The refusal-prefixed prompts of A.8 are training data.
Not tested. Localization is over vocabulary tokens, not weights or ranks.
Not tested. PACT is a token-confidence regularizer during fine-tuning, not training that deepens alignment.

missing.what: Vanilla SFT on AGNEWS (P=10%) with Persuasive-Jailbreaker prompts injected, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. ASR is SR 96.81, JB 54.50, HB 95.50, against Initial 0.32/3.00/9.50 (Table 6).
Vanilla SFT on Refusal-prefixed PJD harmful data mixed into AGNEWS (P=10%), Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. ASR is SR 96.49, JB 57.50, HB 95.00.

SFT on AGNEWS with P=10% harmful plus 500 extra safe examples, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. ASR stays high: SR 15.65, JB 46.00, HB 84.50. This shows that adding safe data only partly blunts harmful-FT erosion.

record.verdict_notes: The harmful data is mixed into task data rather than forming a pure harmful set, and training uses LoRA rank 8 for 3 epochs. The judge is Llama-Guard-3-8B, with Beaver-Dam-7B as a cross-check only for PACT and the baselines. No uncertainty is reported. Llama-3.1-8B Initial accuracy differs between Table 3 (73.39) and Table 6 (75.90), suggesting the settings differ slightly. The paper cites the V3 source (Qi et al. 2024) but does not test first-token concentration. Its 'first 5–10 tokens' remark about refusal prefixes is an unquantified observation.

versions.untested_parts: The main settings use 250 or 500 harmful examples in 5,000-example datasets; the paper does not test every few-example to few-hundred-example quantity.
The benign-only comparison is reported for AGNEWS on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct; it does not establish the effect across all models or data choices.
No per-position KL divergence between aligned and base models on harmful prompts is reported.
No inference-time compliant opening, adversarial suffix, or decoding-change bypass experiment is reported.
The study intervenes on safety-token logits, not on a small set of weights or ranks.
The study does not test whether data or a training objective causes safety alignment to be shallow.
PACT constrains safety-token confidence during fine-tuning, but the study does not test training that spreads safety beyond the opening tokens.

relationships.condition: Vanilla LoRA SFT with 5–10% (250–500) AdvBench harmful examples mixed into GSM8K, SST-2 or AGNEWS, on Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.1-8B, Llama-3.2-1B and Gemma-2-9B instruct models, judged by Llama-Guard-3-8B
relationships.reason: ASR rises from 0–16% at Initial to 46–95% after SFT across all models, tasks and benchmarks (r1–r21). Safety rate declines over epochs (r29). Appendix Tables 10/12 show the same pattern; these results are not in the rows.
relationships.display_finding: Attack success rose from 0–16% initially to 46–95% after SFT across all models, tasks and benchmarks, and the safety rate kept falling over epochs; appendix tables show the same pattern.

relation.reason: Its own vanilla-SFT results directly test V1 and V2.

tranche.reason: The study directly measures harmful compliance after supervised fine-tuning with harmful or benign data, matching the original method and behavioral measure.

source_check.notes: Table 1 names Qwen2.5-7B, defined as the base model in §2.1, but its surrounding interpretation refers to safety-aligned behavior; retain this checkpoint ambiguity. Vocabulary-token interventions do not establish positional KL concentration or localization in weights.

statements.correction: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct; AGNEWS; P=0%; 5,000 examples; LoRA rank 8; three epochs; Llama-Guard-3-8B judge; StrongREJECT ASR 1.60%→1.28%; JailbreakBench 3.00%→2.50%; HarmBench 7.00%→8.00%; uncertainty and significance tests not reported.
statements.problem: The AGNEWS numbers and training conditions are correct, but the blanket negligible-effect reading is not established by the paper. HarmBench increases slightly while the other two benchmarks decrease.
